Let the side length of each large square be \(1\), so its area is \(1\).

**Figure I:**  
The inner diamond connects the midpoints of the large square, so its diagonals are both \(1\), giving area
\[
\frac12\cdot 1\cdot 1=\frac12.
\]
The small central square joins the midpoints of the diamond’s sides, so its side length is \(\frac12\), and its area is
\[
\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac14.
\]
Thus
\[
S_I=\frac12-\frac14=\frac14.
\]

**Figure II:**  
Using coordinates, the shaded triangle has vertices
\[
(0,0),\quad \left(\frac12,1\right),\quad \left(1,\frac12\right).
\]
Its area is
\[
S_{II}=\frac12\left|\frac12\cdot\frac12-1\cdot1\right|
=\frac12\cdot\frac34
=\frac38.
